surprise: probe: label-use lookup took 52 µs at 1K turns and 437–478 µs at 1M (9×); a per-lookup sum over every use breaks TP-T16
resolution: compute ink in time independent of a label's use count (recent uses exact, older folded into an aggregate as in Petrov 2006); rank checked against the naive reference
clause: ink is computed in time independent of a label's use count; ranking equals the differential reference's outside the deadband

surprise: probe: Parakeet transcribes numbers as digits ('340') while owners often type them as words ('three forty')
resolution: number words and digits are one symbol for matching; rendered text unchanged
clause: a number in words and the same number in digits are one symbol for matching; what is rendered stays as written

surprise: probe: Playwright MCP 0.0.86 exposes 25 tools with 21.8 KB of definitions
resolution: keep browser tool definitions inside the browser sub-agent; the main band carries one line for browse
clause: browser tool definitions live only in the browser sub-agent's context

surprise: probe: Playwright MCP snapshot text differed by a few bytes between identical runs
resolution: compare snapshots by content in tests; never byte for byte
clause: browser tests compare snapshot content, not bytes

surprise: probe: the sherpa-onnx 2.0.3 pip wheel's Piper voices fail with no espeak frontend
resolution: generate synthetic speech fixtures with espeak-ng at test time (two distinct voices)
clause: synthetic speech fixtures are generated with espeak-ng at test time

surprise: probe: Playwright MCP 0.0.86 negotiates protocol 2025-11-25, not 2026-07-28
resolution: the MCP client accepts 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 servers
clause: the MCP client accepts servers negotiating 2025-11-25 as well as 2026-07-28

surprise: Omi firmware (main, Nov 2026) reports codec 21 (opusFS320: 320 samples = 20 ms per frame, OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_LOWDELAY so CELT-only, 32 kbps VBR), not the 20 the constitution's src.omi names
resolution: the codec id the device reports selects the frame size (21 → 320, 20 → 160 samples) and libopus decodes both; CELT-only rules out a SILK-only pure-Go decoder
clause: frame size follows the reported codec id (21 → 320 samples, 20 → 160); both decode with libopus

surprise: Omi's offline storage is now a ring/custody record format (firmware transport.c storage records; app wals/sdcard_wal_sync.dart), not a flat file of frames
resolution: the app's port of Omi's storage sync reads the frames out; it uploads them length-prefixed (u16 LE + frame) and the server acknowledges the sha256 of that body once durable
clause: an offline upload is u16-length-prefixed Opus frames; its acknowledgement is the sha256 of the body, sent only after the body is durable

surprise: Anthropic's preserved thinking (Opus 5.5, accounts created after 2026-08-31) rejects a replayed thinking block whose prefix changed; removing all thinking blocks is allowed
resolution: TP's rules already fit: within an exchange the request only grows and thinking passes back unchanged; when it closes all thinking leaves together
clause: within an exchange each request extends the previous one byte for byte; thinking blocks leave only all together, when the exchange closes

surprise: the sherpa-onnx Go binding links its shared libraries with an rpath into the build machine's module cache, and a cgo build on Ubuntu 24.04 needs glibc newer than Debian 12's
resolution: the release ships bin/ and lib/ with rpath $ORIGIN/../lib, built on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35)
clause: the release binary loads its speech libraries from $ORIGIN/../lib and is built against glibc 2.35

surprise: with even edit costs, a real word one edit from an often-used known word is cheaper as label + change than fresh at its English frequency (card 13.15 bits fresh; cart pointer + one 9.08-bit edit below it)
resolution: a word the English list holds is never recorded as another word (endings excepted); MDL decides only for words outside the list, with no more edits than the word's fresh cost covers
clause: a word in the ordinary-English list is never a near-match of a different word; for any other word, label + change wins only when shorter in bits than the word fresh

surprise: Petrov's single aggregate (latest use exact, the rest as one evenly spread mass with mean d) misranked irregular histories by 8% (past the 5% deadband), and one mean d inside a^−d underestimates by Jensen's inequality
resolution: uses fold into time buckets that merge only while width ≤ (deadband / d) × age and (spread of d) × ln(age) ≤ deadband, each integrated with the Euler–Maclaurin end terms; buckets grow with the logarithm of a label's uses (237 at 10K, ~414 at 1M)
clause: ink is a sum over deadband-bounded buckets, never over every use; its ranking equals the exact sum's outside the deadband

surprise: weighting τ by the store's own word information let repetition move trust: every repeat shifts the frequencies the weights come from
resolution: τ weights each word by its ordinary-English information, which no write changes; records are read from the innermost symbol around a word that has one, since labels formed later carry none
clause: τ moves only when an outcome is charged; its word weights are fixed (English information)

surprise: the opening fold was checked on the request without the spotlight it would carry: an opening request reached 16295 tokens against B = 16000
resolution: the fold check counts the request with its spotlight, and the spotlight is recomputed after a fold
clause: the request that opens an exchange is counted with its spotlight before the fold decision, and never exceeds B

surprise: the store serializes on one connection; a query issued while a cursor was still open waited on itself (assembler ranking deadlocked)
resolution: every cursor is read whole and closed before anything else queries
clause: no query runs while a cursor on the store is open

surprise: a landing scored against a heard body that already held its own words gave those words a high chance in themselves (about 5 bits), so nothing could light; and a small heard body makes even a never-heard word likely (a 7-word line in 450 words: 6 bits)
resolution: a landing is scored against the heard body as it stood before it; its uses are recorded after; tests carry a week-sized heard body
clause: a landing's own words never count toward their own chance

surprise: synchronous=FULL on every statement made each grammar row an fsync (about 0.2 s per exchange)
resolution: the connection runs synchronous=NORMAL in WAL mode (committed frames survive a killed process); seals, heard rows and calls marked running commit through Durable with FULL, which fsyncs the log and every commit before it
clause: a sealed turn, a heard row and a call marked running are committed with a full fsync before the caller goes on

surprise: an incremental sleep pass (greedy respelling, then folding labels used once) oscillated: a label formed for a pair seen twice could end up used once after greedy respelling, fold, and form again; and TP-T12's folding assumes Sequitur's n-ary rules while labels here are pairs
resolution: the sleep pass rebuilds labels from the rows by Re-Pair (every non-overlapping occurrence of the most frequent pair, repeatedly), so each label is born with two occurrences and keeps them through its holders; a label's occurrences count every place its expansion appears; unneeded labels are retired, not deleted
clause: after each sleep pass no pair of symbols appears twice in the rows' spellings, every active label occurs at least twice counting through the labels that hold it, and the pass depends only on the rows

surprise: 'an owner message after the draft was shown' compared the phone's send time with the server's clock; on one clock they can tie, across clocks they can invert
resolution: the draft and the owner's message each keep the id of the event that showed or received them; the event log's order decides
clause: a draft runs only when an owner message received after its draft event opened the exchange; the order is the event log's, not a clock's

surprise: A04's 'success closes the loop' looked for a request without the open redline, but requests within an exchange only append, so the earlier rounds' spotlights keep showing it
resolution: a round's own spotlight is the part its request adds; the loop is closed in the first round after the success whose request adds no open redline
clause: A04 success_closes_loop: the request after the successful step adds no open redline to what the exchange already carries

surprise: A14's owner repeated 'post the weekly order' over a waiting draft of the same bytes, so the call ran as that draft's approval before standing was consulted; standing never showed
resolution: none needed in the loop: a draft is per bytes and the owner's word over it runs it (D6); standing is per step. The scenario's pre-grant draft carries other bytes than the standing call
clause: standing is consulted for a call only when no waiting draft holds its exact bytes

surprise: readings from beyond the machine were rendered like any tool result, so the model could not tell a PDF's words from the box's own output
resolution: a reading whose outside flag is set rides in its tool_result wrapped in <outside>…</outside>; the system prompt names the wrapper
clause: every tool_result whose reading came from beyond the machine is wrapped in <outside>

surprise: a mail draft stored the agent's call, so its Date and Message-ID could only be made at send time and the bytes sent would differ from those shown
resolution: a tool may compose its payload when drafted (tools.Composer); the draft keeps the call to match a repeat and the composed message as its payload and shown text
clause: a drafted mail's payload is the complete message, Date and Message-ID included, and the bytes SMTP receives equal the shown text

surprise: an install that failed (its service exited) left its accounts, linger flags and user units behind, and every later install on the host reused those accounts, whose homes pointed at the dead root
resolution: a fresh install that fails uninstalls what it made and reports the server's journal; the acceptance harness registers its uninstall before installing
clause: after a failed fresh install the host holds no Plebian account, unit, linger flag or root

surprise: a message or calendar entry landed as one heard line, and the heard wake needs three lit lines, so no mail, text or entry coming due could ever wake the agent
resolution: messages and entries land one heard line per line of text that holds words, each from its sender at its wall time; the original keeps every byte
clause: a message's heard row holds one line per non-empty text line; a three-line mail answering an open question opens one turn on a lived-in box

surprise: a sendBeacon usually skipped page-level Fetch interception (keepalive requests leave through the browser process), so a beacon could reach the site
resolution: the guard also intercepts at the browser target, for Ping resources only (so no other request is paused twice), and drops them there
clause: a beacon is dropped whichever process sends it; no request is paused at two levels

surprise: the audit found a networked run shares the host network, where Chromium's DevTools listens on loopback with no credential, so a run could drive the owner's signed-in browser around the guard
resolution: time separation: a networked run refuses to start while the box's browser is up; the browser closes when no browse task, live view or held request needs it (G034)
clause: no networked tool run executes while the box's browser process is running

surprise: the live view's promise that the agent waits while the owner holds the wheel was not kept: the browse sub-agent never looked
resolution: before each sub-agent action the browse task waits while the owner holds the wheel
clause: no agent action runs while the owner holds the wheel

surprise: readings recovered after a crash opened their exchange as a job, so the draft rule lost the heard and word-to-go-out state of the exchange they answer
resolution: a readings inbound carries the opener of the exchange whose calls it answers; a question code raises is not heard-opened
clause: a recovered reading's exchange keeps its original opener

surprise: single-file speech models fetched as root landed 0600 (CreateTemp's mode), so sherpa-onnx aborted under the server account and every install with speech failed to start
resolution: a fetched single-file model is made readable by others before it is renamed into place
clause: the server's account can read every installed speech model

surprise: the installer made the browser directory as root, so the server account could not create Chromium's profile and the box's browser never started in an installed root
resolution: install creates browser/ and browser/profile owned by the server account; Launch returns the profile error and Chromium's startup stderr
clause: the installed server can start the box's browser

surprise: systemd-run from the server failed with EPERM (systemd 249 bus_check_peercred: the user bus found through the environment belonged to another uid)
resolution: deploy's systemd-run and the helper's systemctl calls name the account's own runtime directory by uid; a failure records the uid
clause: a signed deploy reaches the server account's own user manager

surprise: Omi firmware at the cloned head (3.0.24) speaks a third storage protocol G003 does not name: a ring buffer (3.0.20+) reusing opcodes 0x10 info, 0x11 read, 0x12 advance with meanings unlike the 3.0.17-3.0.19 multi-file 0x10 list, 0x11 read, 0x12 delete; Omi's app picks by DIS firmware revision, not by what the device answers
resolution: the simulator picks its protocol by firmware revision as the app does: ring (ported from storage.c, sd_card.c, custody.c) for 3.0.20+, multi-file for 3.0.17-3.0.19, the length list before; default 3.0.24 (omi.conf CONFIG_BT_DIS_FW_REV_STR)
clause: the Omi simulator serves offline storage over the protocol its firmware revision selects: ring for 3.0.20 and later, multi-file for 3.0.17-3.0.19, the length list before

surprise: current Omi firmware reports codec id 21 (opusFS320: 320-sample, 20 ms frames, at most 160 bytes), not 20 as src.omi's units line says
resolution: the simulator and speech fixture default to codec 21 and also serve codec 20 (160-sample frames, at most 80 bytes) as Omi's app models it
clause: src.omi audio is codec 21 by default (config.h CODEC_ID); codec 20 is the older 10 ms framing

surprise: the firmware streams no live audio below an ATT MTU of 100 (config.h MINIMAL_PACKET_SIZE): until the phone's MTU exchange the frames go to offline storage, and the packet number advances once per notification, not once per frame
resolution: the simulator holds MTU 23 until the phone exchanges (result min(asked, 498), omi.conf CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_TX_MTU) and routes frames as the pusher does
clause: live Omi audio needs a negotiated MTU of at least 100; a frame larger than MTU-6 bytes arrives as consecutive packet numbers with fragment indexes 0,1,...

surprise: the tailnet listener took the localhost listener's port, which the kernel picks fresh at every start, so the address a phone paired with changed on every restart, deploy or reboot
resolution: the tailnet side listens on HTTP's default port 80 (RFC 9110 §4.2.1) on tsnet's own netstack, so it collides with nothing on the host and the paired address is stable
clause: the paired address survives a restart
kill_test: none in CI (CI runs --no-tailnet); first-run checklist line 6

surprise: when no window was due on the current page day (the step had already run today), the clock returned no time to look again, so the running loop slept through the next day's window; the unit test stepped the loop by hand and never saw it, and A13 failed in CI
resolution: with steps on record and nothing due, the clock looks again at the next 4 am page cut
clause: the running loop wakes for a due window on its own
kill_test: tests/loop/clock_cut_test.go TestClockWakesTheRunningLoop (seen red: clock_cut_test.go:76: the running loop opened 0 clock turns on the third night)

surprise: Flutter 3.50 deprecates package:flutter/material.dart in favour of the material_ui package; `flutter analyze` fails on the deprecation info
resolution: material_ui 1.11.0 imported everywhere
clause: the app's source passes flutter analyze on the pinned Flutter

surprise: a projection widget reused for another path (Journal Days -> Taps) built the new screen from the previous path's JSON and threw
resolution: Loaded drops its data whenever its path or query changes
clause: every control on every screen does what its label says against the real API; no screen is a placeholder

surprise: a tap dot's 'tapped' label merged into the ribbon's semantics node, so TalkBack never read it alone
resolution: TapDot is its own semantics container
clause: every control has a TalkBack label; a tap's dot is read aloud as tapped

surprise: a foreground service alone does not keep Dart running: FlutterActivity destroys its engine with the activity
resolution: one cached FlutterEngine per process (MainActivity uses it and never destroys it); LinkService (type connectedDevice) keeps the process and starts the engine if the system restarts the service; flutter_foreground_task (Omi's choice) would put the links in a second isolate
clause: every message the agent starts raises an Android notification through the service's own server link (no push service)

surprise: the owner's message event carries client_msg_id, not the id POST /v1/messages answers with
resolution: a sent message stays shown until its event (matched by client_msg_id) arrives
clause: messages and audio queue while the server is unreachable and send in order when it returns

surprise: Omi's own reassembler (wav_bytes.dart storeFramePacket) compares `index != lastPacketIndex + 1`, so the frame after the u16 packet counter wraps 65535 -> 0 is dropped
resolution: the port compares modulo 2^16: `packet != (_last + 1) & 0xFFFF` (app/lib/device/omi_protocol.dart FrameAssembler)
clause: packet numbers wrap at 65535 without dropping audio

surprise: Omi's app has no BLE plugin in its pubspec: it drives BLE through its own native Pigeon bridge (NativeBleTransport, BleHostApi); flutter_blue_plus is under a non-OSI license
resolution: BleTransport on universal_ble 3.3.0 (BSD-3-Clause) behind the one DeviceTransport interface; G039
clause: the transport sits behind one interface

surprise: current Omi firmware (3.0.20+, the simulator's default 3.0.24) speaks a third storage protocol, a ring buffer, reusing command bytes 0x10/0x11/0x12 (info/read/advance) that the multi-file firmware uses for list/read/delete
resolution: all three paths ported (legacy length list, multi-file, ring), chosen by firmware revision then by what the control characteristic answers; delete = ring advance / file delete / legacy clear, each only on the server's sha256
clause: an offline file is deleted from the Omi only after the server confirms its hash

surprise: a new BLE link forgets the MTU and every CCC subscription (the simulator resets both on reconnect), so audio and storage notifications stop after the Omi comes back in range
resolution: OmiDevice.link() redoes the MTU exchange, the four subscriptions and the time sync on every reconnect, then the stored audio syncs; the CCC write is its own awaited call on the transport so no storage command races it
clause: a background service keeps the Omi link and the server link alive with the app closed

surprise: the server as built (server/audio/audio.go File) takes an offline file as u16 LE length + one Opus frame each and reads X-Omi-File-Timestamp as device milliseconds; API.md says device seconds, and the coordinator's note says each packet carries its ms timestamp
resolution: the app parses the device's stored blocks into Opus frames, splits a read into runs at a device-clock step over 60 s (Omi ringRecordGapBreakSeconds), and posts one file per run with the run's start in ms; the Omi is touched only after every run's sha256 matches
clause: each offline file is acknowledged to the app with its sha256 only once it is durable in the blob store

surprise: correction to L0031: the browser directory was already the server account's (install's directory table); run 45978542120 showed the real cause once Launch reported Chromium's stderr: 'chrome_crashpad_handler: --database is required', the crash reporter finding no database directory under the service account
resolution: Chromium starts with --disable-crash-reporter and --crash-dumps-dir under its profile; L0031's ownership change stays (harmless) but was not the cause
clause: the installed server can start the box's browser
kill_test: tests/acceptance A12 owner_signed_in_live (pending the next CI run)

surprise: lookup matched a query's words only within one line, while speech detection splits a spoken sentence at a pause; A09 drew no reply in run 45978542120, consistent with lookup finding nothing (the same exchange replies at the loop level with the row present)
resolution: lookup matches the words across a row's lines (the named speaker's lines when who is given)
clause: a heard fact asked by text is found whatever the pauses in it
kill_test: tests/underlay/underlay_test.go TestLookupAcrossLines (seen red: underlay_test.go:197: lookup for words split across a stretch's lines found [])
